sentences.text: Tambatitanis is an extinct genus of sauropod dinosaur classified as a titanosauriform, possibly a titanosaurian.
The genus Tambatitanis is known from a single species, Tambatitanis amicitiae, represented by a partial skeleton.
The tail indicates a total length of between 10 and 15 meters.
The chevron of the first tail vertebra is the longest of all known sauropods relative to body size.
In 2016, Gregory S. Paul estimated the animal was around 14 meters long and weighed approximately 4 tons.
The holotype specimen of Tambatitanis was discovered in August 2006 by amateur paleontologists Shigeru Murakami and Kiyoshi Adachi.
The fossil was originally named 'Tamba-Ryu' before being formally published in 2014.
Haruo Saegusa and Tadahiro Ikeda described Tambatitanis amicitiae as a new genus and species in 2014.
It took five years to excavate the fossil from a hard rock site covering an area of six by four meters.
Phylogenetic analysis suggests Tambatitanis belonged to Euhelopodidae, but its specific placement within the group remains uncertain.
An initial cladistic analysis placed Tambatitanis close to Qiaowanlong, Erketu, Euhelopus, Daxiatitan, Tangvayosaurus, and Phuwiangosaurus.
Reviewers noted that initial results were preliminary and that the skull of Tambatitanis is more similar to that of Titanosauridae.
Tambatitanis lived during the Lower Cretaceous (lower Albian) in what is now Japan.
Tambatitanis amicitiae lived during the mid-Cretaceous, between 112 and 109 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
The time range for Tambatitanis is the Albian, from 113.2 to 110.1 million years ago.
